gate1.BARReach: Binder/snapshot/proof preparation is a historical actual BAR path. Current vector-specific length/allocation distribution is unmeasured, and no extra collector is requested.
counterexamples: Singleton temporary vector currently has one owning allocation that is moved into persistent entry. Inline scratch followed by vector destination construction still needs that destination allocation and can add copies.

Moving snapshotResources into groupResources before snapshots->remember leaves the later snapshot with moved-from elements. Both independent destination owners require the current copy or a separate ownership redesign.
A first valid proof does not imply every later proof is valid. Reserving a full multi-element capacity may use more bytes on a late failure even if allocation counts do not increase.
Reserving64 for group capture before any valid append allocates in otherwise-empty/rejected paths; repeated reserve(size+nextBinding) can defeat geometric capacity growth.
gate1.decision: A narrowly bounded reserve proposal may proceed to source review; no blanket profit guarantee and no FPS pre-proof required.

narrowProposalBoundary: Only existing temporary std::vector collection of known bounded cardinality, preferably bufferProofs/textureProofs/snapshotResources with existing<=16 admission.
After the first valid resource/proof and existing eligibility/preflight, reserve exact bounded total only for total>1 and insufficient capacity.
Keep group/recording/texture fast hits, negative rejection and count0/1 free of new allocations; preserve already-owned partial-vector capacity after clear.
Leave move-to-persistent remember contracts, budgets, resource identity and full/partial result/callback order unchanged.
Explicitly accept a bounded temporary capacity increase when later validation fails; this alone is not a rejection.
No global scratch, new persistent cache, inline-container conversion, added collector, broad pass/sync changes or new source scope.

gate1.stop: If proposal cannot remove an actual growth allocation without additional passes, duplicates persistent allocation/copy, widens resource ownership or changes validation/result order, leave this site unchanged.
